items.title: Bob Wilber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998
items.q: And Ernie says, “Look if he doesn’t show, you’ve got to go on in his place.”

ctx.x: Yeah. It shows a great respect for the music.

Well the same thing happened when — remember the famous Louis Armstrong 1947 Town Hall concert, a concert which was the basis for the Louis Armstrong All Stars. In other words with Louis switching from the big band format to a small band format. I was living with Sidney at the time in Brooklyn and so the concert was one of those 5:30 starts at Town Hall on Saturday afternoon. So I said to Sid, “I think I’ll go in town and catch a movie this afternoon, so I’ll see you backstage at Town Hall around five o’clock.”…

This is a band with Armstrong, Hackett, Jack Teagarden, Big Sid Catlett, Bob Haggart. I’m not ready for this yet. No I can’t, I just can’t. So anyway the concert went ahead, and it was a big success, it was recorded, and the promoters, they had to beg Joe Glaser to let them use Louis without his whole band. He was dead set against it. “You want Louis Armstrong, you’ve got to take the whole band.” “No we just want Louis, just this one concert.” Well anyway, Glaser saw the tremendous applause and appreciation of…

items.title: Bob Wilber Interview, 1961-05-01
items.q: Ernie Anderson and Fred Robbins were saying where is Sidney and they wanted me to go on and play

ctx.x: and well what happened was Sidney was going on a subway to the concert and got sick and was just lying there practically unconscious and he rode around the subway for hours people thought he was drunk you know and nobody knew where is Sidney I remember being backstage at this thing and Ernie Anderson and Fred Robbins were saying where is Sidney and they wanted me to go on and play and I wouldn't do it because I you'd be upset too naturally well I was upset too and I also felt I wasn't ready for this I wasn't…
yeah that's pretty early when was that? forty-seven
